message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations consult an attorney or your local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What You’re Generally Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|-----------------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written receipt of the deposit.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if you disagree. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control). | • Report problems in writing (email or letter).
• If unresolved, you may withhold rent or repair and deduct (see below). | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix a major problem within a reasonable time, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, provided you give notice and keep receipts. | • Give written notice, keep copies of all correspondence, and document the repair costs. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if needed. | | **Notice to Vacate** | • Landlord must give at least 30 days’ written notice to terminate a month‑to‑month tenancy.
• For a fixed‑term lease, the landlord can only terminate for cause (e.g., non‑payment, violation of lease). | • Keep copies of all notices received. | | **Privacy & Entry** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours’ written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | • Ask for a written notice and keep a record of entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected under the Texas Fair Housing Act and federal Fair Housing Act: no discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing for any term longer than one year. | • Review the lease carefully before signing; ask questions about ambiguous clauses. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Landlord may deduct for: unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, cleaning if agreed upon, and replacement of lost keys. | • Dispute any deduction you believe is unjustified. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the Texas eviction procedure (notice, filing, court order). | • Respond to notices promptly; consider seeking legal aid if facing eviction. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord may require you to pay utilities unless otherwise specified. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Usually requires landlord’s written consent; some leases prohibit subletting. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must maintain common areas (hallways, elevators, parking). | • Report maintenance issues in writing. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Document any disturbances and notify the landlord. | ### Practical Steps to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, receipts, emails, text messages, and any written communication with the landlord. 2. **Use Written Notices** – Whenever possible, send notices via certified mail or email with read receipts. 3. **Know the Timeline** – Texas law sets specific time frames for repairs, notice periods, and deposit returns. 4. **Seek Assistance Early** – If you encounter a problem, contact a local tenant‑rights group (e.g., Texas Tenants Union) or a legal aid office before the issue escalates. 5. **Keep Records of Repairs** – If you perform repairs, keep receipts and photos to support a repair‑and‑deduct claim. --- #### Quick Reference Resources | Resource | What It Offers | How to Access | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Property Code** | Statutory rights and obligations | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | File discrimination complaints | https://www.tchra.org/ | | **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** | Fair housing complaints | https://www.hud.gov/ | | **Texas Legal Services Center** | Free legal assistance | https://www.texaslawhelp.org/ | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** | Advocacy, workshops | Search online for “tenant rights Texas” | Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detail on any particular area, or if you need help drafting a notice or understanding a specific clause in your lease.
